title: Dominic and the Vow
premise: Elodie Reyes has spent a decade keeping her head down in the small town of Marrow Creek, running its last bookshop and raising her daughter alone after the man she loved at twenty-three—Dominic Vale—chose a career over her and vanished. When a freak snowstorm traps them both in the shop overnight with his estranged teenage nephew, whom Dominic is reluctantly guardians of, old wounds and new tenderness collide. As Elodie fights to save her best friend's failing bakery next door—the heart of their found family—and Dominic wrestles with a secret about why he really left, they must decide whether loyalty to the people they've become matters more than the truth of who they were. The story ends with the bakery saved through a joint community effort, Dominic choosing to stay and co-parent his nephew in Marrow Creek, and Elodie forgiving herself for believing she was easy to leave.
about_author: Theo Underhill is the pen name of a former small-town bookseller who spent fifteen years shelving romance novels before writing one. They live in a drafty house full of paperbacks and insist every good love story needs a snowstorm.

chapters.title: The Last Warm Shelf
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A quiet October morning in Pages & Ink as Elodie opens the shop, establishes her careful routines with daughter Wren, and learns the bakery next door may not survive winter. Emotional beat: contentment built on avoidance, cracked by the first hint of change.

chapters.title: A Stranger with Familiar Hands
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Dominic Vale walks into the bookshop to buy a gift for his nephew and freezes when he sees her. Ten years collapse in a single exchange of stilted politeness. Emotional beat: shock masked as civility, the past arriving without permission.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV (Elodie's best friend, the baker). Marisol clocks Dominic immediately and warns Elodie, while revealing the bakery's lease crisis in full. Emotional beat: protective anger and the weight of a friendship that functions as family.

chapters.title: Guardian, Reluctantly
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic explains to himself why he's back: his late sister named him guardian of Theo, sixteen, who resents being uprooted. He tells himself Marrow Creek is temporary. Emotional beat: guilt wearing the costume of practicality.

chapters.title: Overdue
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Theo starts haunting the bookshop after school, and Elodie recognizes the loneliness beneath his surliness. She gives him a job shelving books. Emotional beat: unexpected tenderness toward the boy who carries Dominic's face.

chapters.title: The Lease Runs Out
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The landlord delivers an ultimatum on the bakery; Elodie organizes a fundraiser that draws the whole town, including an awkwardly helpful Dominic. Emotional beat: found family rallying, with rivalry sparking between two stubborn helpers.

chapters.title: Snowfall Warning
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The forecast turns ugly; Dominic offers to drive Elodie home and they argue the whole way, old grievances surfacing like ice under tires. Emotional beat: anger that is unmistakably intimacy in disguise.

chapters.title: Stranded
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The storm closes the road; Elodie, Dominic, and Theo are trapped in the bookshop overnight with candles, wine, and nowhere to hide. Emotional beat: forced proximity dissolving a decade of distance.

chapters.title: The Best Mistake of Our Twenties
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. By firelight, the truth of their breakup finally surfaces—he chose a job offer in another country and never told her he'd been offered a local one too. Emotional beat: confession, fury, and the first honest look in ten years.

chapters.title: Morning After the Storm
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Snowbound streets, awkward dawn, Wren asking why Mommy's eyes are red. Elodie insists nothing has changed while everything has. Emotional beat: denial as self-protection.

chapters.title: Theo's Side of It
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, having eavesdropped all night, confronts his uncle about running away again, revealing he read his mother's letters and knows Dominic promised her he'd come back here someday. Emotional beat: a teenager forcing adults into honesty.

chapters.title: Baking Bad News
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The landlord sells the building to a developer; the fundraiser money won't be enough. Marisol begins packing boxes, and Elodie refuses to let her. Emotional beat: grief and defiance side by side.

chapters.title: Second Chances Have Terrible Timing
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic asks Elodie to dinner, properly this time. She says no—not because she doesn't want to, but because she doesn't trust herself to survive another leaving. Emotional beat: longing barricaded behind scar tissue.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A quiet chapter: Elodie rereads her old letters to Dominic and confronts how she made herself small after he left, telling herself invisibility was safety. Wren asks why she never dances anymore. Emotional beat: turning inward, forgiveness beginning with herself.

chapters.title: An Offer with Strings
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic learns the developer buying the building is his old firm's biggest client. He could walk away—or use his leverage. He risks his career by pushing the firm to sell the bakery space to the town instead. Emotional beat: loyalty finally outweighing ambition.

chapters.title: Rumors and Ribbon
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Town gossip twists Dominic's meetings with the developer; Elodie hears he's involved in the sale and assumes betrayal. The fundraiser falls apart mid-planning. Emotional beat: misunderstanding weaponized by old fear.

chapters.title: The Letter He Never Sent
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds the unsent letter Dominic wrote Elodie ten years ago and leaves it on the bookshop counter. Elodie reads it: he came back once, saw her happy, and couldn't bear to disrupt her life. Emotional beat: devastating reframe of a decade of hurt.

chapters.title: Everything on the Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax. At the nearly-empty bakery, Elodie and Dominic have it out—every silence, every assumption, every year apart—while Theo and Marisol refuse to let either of them storm off. Emotional beat: the truth, finally louder than pride.

chapters.title: The Town That Stayed
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. With the developer deal secured, the town buys the building as a community co-op; the bakery is saved and the bookshop's lease renewed alongside it. Emotional beat: belonging proven, not just claimed.

chapters.title: First Date, Second Attempt
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic takes Elodie dancing in the closed bookstore aisle, Wren asleep on a beanbag, Theo grudgingly DJ-ing. No grand gestures—just presence. Emotional beat: joy allowed, cautiously, completely.

chapters.title: Vows, Informal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Not a wedding but something better: a Sunday dinner where Dominic, Theo, Wren, Elodie, and Marisol argue over casserole like they've always done it. Dominic makes a quiet vow to stay, witnessed by everyone who matters. Emotional beat: found family formalized in flour and noise.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Spring. Elodie flips the shop sign to OPEN, watches Theo walk Theo-the-nephew to school, and catches her reflection in the window—someone who stayed visible and survived it. Final beat: second chances were always hers to claim.
